meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You asked for this meeting, Hale. I have until 4:40, so tell me who decided on the zero, and why I found out after Owen did.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it, or did he find out the same way the rest of his class did?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
You still haven't answered me, Hale: was Owen heard before that zero went in, because 4.1 says he comes first and 4.2 says I come before any mark.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
I'm writing down Act 3, Scene 2. Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every day, Hale, so a wrong line is a careless student, not proof of anything.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

That's 4.4, and I'll want it in an email today. Before I agree to anything, Hale, does bringing in the vice-principal mean the office already has this, and is that zero still sitting in the gradebook right now?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you apologised for entering Owen's zero before calling me, and you offered a supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 in your room on Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising. I still require written confirmation that nothing about this is on Owen's record or with the office, the status of the zero in the gradebook, and an answer to whether Owen was heard before the mark went in. I expect that in writing today, as I said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her fallback position, because your offer of a private rewrite with nothing on his record met her core demand; she had not yet agreed to the rewrite and still wants it in writing, confirmation the office does not have the matter, and an answer on whether Owen was heard first. That is close to the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You laid out the rewrite terms exactly as the procedure states them, with a day, a time and a supervisor, which gave her something concrete to hold you to.
What cost ground: You never answered whether Owen was heard before the zero went in, though she asked twice, so the procedural gap stayed open the whole meeting.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the whole essay between 11:31 PM and 11:58 PM the night before it was due, which landed very close to that kind of late night and is why she went straight to procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether Owen was heard before the zero, answer that directly before showing the version history, so your evidence lands without an open procedural question behind it.
